schools.name: Constantine Bay Surf School
schools.note: Group, private and private-group lessons, from tasters to improver sessions. Coaches are qualified beach lifeguards and use local knowledge to pick the best of the seven bays for conditions.

schools.name: George's Surf School
schools.base: Meets at Constantine Bay (main base at Polzeath)
schools.note: Private one-to-one and small-group lessons for all levels, children's lessons, family sessions and video coaching.

hire.name: The Pit Surf Shop
hire.base: The Airfield, St Merryn (PL28 8PU), a short drive inland from Constantine
hire.note: Hires foam and epoxy surfboards, bodyboards, kids' and adult wetsuits, boots, gloves, hoods and fins, and now delivers hire kit.

shops.name: The Pit Surf Shop
shops.note: Open all year, with a big bodyboard range plus fins, leashes, wetsuit hoods, changing robes and accessories, and a board repair section. It's the closest surf shop we could confirm to Constantine.

lessonsIntro: Constantine Bay is one of the best-quality waves around Padstow, but it's a beach to learn on with a school rather than on your own. Local coaches use the beach when it's suitable and move to sheltered spots nearby when it isn't.

text: Constantine is a sandy bay about three miles from Padstow, just south of Booby's Bay, known for powerful, good-quality waves. Visit Cornwall lists it as suitable for experienced surfers only, which is why lessons here are run by local schools who know when it's safe. Constantine Bay Surf School says it uses local knowledge of the seven bays to find suitable surf on the day.

The hazards are real: Visit Cornwall warns of strong rips, hidden rocks and a large rocky reef at the southern end, and says the beach shelves quickly at high tide. The RNLI reports rip currents at both low and high tide, with bodyboarders drifting a long way out. Lifeguards patrol through the summer, so stay inside the red and yellow flags and never go in alone as a beginner.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Lessons only for beginners
cards.text: Rated for experienced surfers. Beginners should only surf here with a qualified school, and improvers should keep to the patrolled area.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Summer, with lifeguards
cards.text: Lifeguards cover the summer season. The middle of the bay peaks at high tide and the north end works from mid to high tide.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Rips, rocks and the reef
cards.text: Strong rips at low and high tide, hidden rocks, a big reef to the south and a beach that shelves fast at high tide.

hireIntro: There's no confirmed hire on the beach at Constantine, but The Pit Surf Shop at St Merryn, a short drive away, hires and delivers kit.

text: Constantine's waves have more push than nearby Harlyn, so beginners should stick to a big foam board in the white water with a school. Confident improvers will want a responsive epoxy board, and The Pit hires both. Sea temperatures on this stretch range from about 9 to 10°C in early March to 15 to 18°C in August.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Foam to start, epoxy to progress
cards.text: A soft foam board for lessons; an epoxy board once you can paddle out and handle stronger waves.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 3/2 or 4/3 in summer, 5/4 in winter
cards.text: Surf-forecast suggests a 4/3 or 3/2 with boots in August and a 5/4 or 5/3 with gloves and boots in early March.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboard with care
cards.text: Bodyboarders have needed rescuing after drifting outside the flags here, so stay between the red and yellow flags.

shopsIntro: Constantine has no surf shop on the beach. The nearest confirmed shop is a short drive inland at St Merryn.
shopsText: The Pit Surf Shop at The Airfield in St Merryn is a few minutes' drive from Constantine and is open all year. It specialises in bodyboards and stocks fins, leashes, wetsuit hoods, robes and accessories, with board repairs listed. Padstow, about three miles away, is the nearest town for other shopping.

lessons.q: Can beginners surf at Constantine Bay?
lessons.a: Only with a school. Visit Cornwall rates the beach for experienced surfers because of strong rips, hidden rocks and a reef, but local schools teach here when conditions suit.
Constantine Bay Surf School is based here, and George's Surf School uses Constantine as a meeting point for some lessons.

lessons.q: What if conditions are too big at Constantine?
lessons.a: Constantine Bay Surf School says it uses local knowledge of the seven bays around Padstow to find suitable surf, so your lesson may move to a nearby beach.

hire.q: Is there surf hire at Constantine Bay?
hire.a: We couldn't confirm any hire on the beach itself. The Pit Surf Shop at St Merryn hires boards and wetsuits and now offers delivery.
The Pit hires foam and epoxy surfboards, bodyboards, kids' and adult wetsuits, boots, gloves, hoods and fins.

shops.a: The Pit Surf Shop at The Airfield, St Merryn, a short drive inland from Constantine.
